audit.whatIsWrong: content.early tells the player that after Yasuo plants Wind Wall they should "wait out its five-second cooldown".
audit.why: Wind Wall's cooldown is 25/23/21/19/17 seconds. Five seconds is not close to any rank. The four-second figure in the kit is the wall's DURATION, and the two have been conflated into a number that is off by a factor of five at rank 1. This is the most dangerous line in the matchup: a Tahm Kench who steps back in after five seconds walks into a wall that is still up with sixteen seconds left on it, loses the Tongue Lash he needed for stacks, and eats the trade. Inverted, the real number is the best news in the lane — a whiffed Wind Wall hands you a 25-second window where your stun threat is live.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall lasts 4s; the cooldown is 25/23/21/19/17s. Bait it, then own the next twenty seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire full layer tracks the wrong champion's ability: breakdown.cooldowns says "- Yasuo Tongue Lash: matchup-defining", dosFull[0] is "Track Yasuo's Tongue Lash before you commit", report[5].t says "Track Yasuo's Tongue Lash", and dosFull[2].d says "Yasuo wastes Tongue Lash". Tongue Lash is Tahm Kench's own Q.
audit.why: Yasuo has no ability called Tongue Lash — his kit is Way of the Wanderer, Steel Tempest, Wind Wall, Sweeping Blade, Last Breath. The template has filled the enemy-cooldown slot with the owner's ability, so every "track it" instruction in the full layer points at a button the player is holding himself. The ability that actually decides this matchup, Wind Wall, is never given a cooldown anywhere in either layer.
audit.corrected: Track Wind Wall (25/23/21/19/17s), Sweeping Blade (0.5/0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1s) and Last Breath (70/50/30s).

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer warns that Abyssal Dive's knockup gives Yasuo a free Last Breath. dosFull[2] is even titled "W-dodge his EQ knockup", actively encouraging W use in the fight.
audit.why: Last Breath "blinks to an Airborne enemy champion". Abyssal Dive "damages and knocks up all enemies in an area". The kit flags them as a matching pair — knockup-enabler on one side, knockup-dependent ult on the other. Tahm Kench's own engage is therefore the cleanest ultimate setup Yasuo will get all game, and it also airbornes any teammate standing in the landing zone. This is the single highest-value unwritten interaction in the matchup and the text currently points the wrong way.
audit.corrected: Never open a fight with Abyssal Dive while Last Breath is up — your knockup is his ult trigger, on you or on whoever you dive next to.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] and spikes[2].text attribute "Phantom Drive" to Yasuo.
audit.why: Phantom Drive belongs to Xayah and Rakan. Yasuo's dash is Sweeping Blade, and its real number is far more useful than the wrong name: 0.5/0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1 seconds, re-castable off any minion, which is exactly why pinning him for three stacks is so hard. The near-miss detector did not flag this because Phantom Drive is not within edit distance of anything in Yasuo's kit.
audit.corrected: Sweeping Blade, 0.5s at rank 1 down to 0.1s at rank 5, off any unit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer asserts Tongue Lash is "Melee on 3 stacks — Wind Wall won't matter for the stun" (breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t), while the content layer says the opposite: "Windwall blocks Tongue Lash cleanly", "never throw Tongue Lash when Windwall is up".
audit.why: The two layers contradict each other on the central question of the matchup, and the full-layer version is an invented mechanic — nothing in Riot's Tongue Lash text makes it melee at three stacks, or changes its behaviour at all beyond adding the stun. A player told Wind Wall does not matter will throw his Q into the wall every time.
audit.corrected: Tongue Lash does not change form at three stacks. Wind Wall matters; play around its cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3].text says "Last Breath can no longer be eaten by Devour if he ults an airborne ally".
audit.why: Last Breath targets an airborne ENEMY champion — Yasuo does not ult allies, so the sentence describes something that cannot happen. The real content that belongs in this slot is the inverse interaction: what makes an airborne target for him is your own Abyssal Dive.
audit.corrected: Last Breath blinks to an airborne enemy. The thing to avoid is handing him one with your own W.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1] and content.early say two An Acquired Taste stacks arm the stun; spikes[0].text and whys[2] sell "stun into Devour" off one stack set.
audit.why: Off by one, then double-spent. Riot's Q text: the stun fires only when the champion ALREADY has 3 stacks, and it consumes them. So two stacks threaten nothing, three stacks arm the next Tongue Lash, and once that stun lands Devour is uncastable because the passive requires three stacks to eat.
audit.corrected: Three stacks arms the stun. The stun and Devour are alternative spenders of the same three stacks.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (Riot Data Dragon 16.15.1) — P and Q descriptions

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid, content.late and whys[4] use "Abyssal Voyage" for global presence.
audit.why: Removed pre-2020 ability. The live W is Abyssal Dive, short-range knockup, 21/20/19/18/17s — and in this matchup specifically it is a liability rather than a tool, because of the Last Breath interaction above.
audit.corrected: No global in the kit. Level 6 is Devour.

edits.before: Early levels are legitimately yours. Your Tongue Lash outranges Yasuo's Steel Tempest and the slow lets you walk down a champion with no reliable escape. At two An Acquired Taste stacks he has to respect you or eat a stun, so he either backs off the wave — giving you free CS — or overcommits and gets devoured into a full combo. The key: never throw Tongue Lash when Windwall is up. If he plants it in the lane, wait out its five-second cooldown, then immediately Q to restart your stack window before he can Steel Tempest his third charge safely.
edits.after: Early levels are legitimately yours. Your Tongue Lash outranges Yasuo's Steel Tempest and the slow lets you walk down a champion with no reliable escape. At three An Acquired Taste stacks the next Tongue Lash stuns, so he either backs off the wave — giving you free CS — or overcommits and gets devoured. The key rule: never throw Tongue Lash while Wind Wall is up. It lasts four seconds but the cooldown is 25s at rank 1 and still 17s at rank 5, so once he plants it that whole window belongs to you.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the flattest part of the lane. Yasuo's Windwall is the single ability that dismantles your kit — it eats your Tongue Lash projectile, resetting your An Acquired Taste progress and leaving you with no stun threat in the trade. He can hold Windwall reactively the moment you step to auto, which means you are fishing for stacks against a champion who can simply walk away through minions on his dash. Play for CS, bait the Windwall on a predicted Tongue Lash bluff, then immediately throw the real one while it is on cooldown. At six Abyssal Voyage gives you global presence, but it does not win this specific duel — it is a tool to help your team while Yasuo builds into crit.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are the flattest part of the lane. Yasuo's Wind Wall is the single ability that dismantles your kit — it eats your Tongue Lash projectile, stalling your An Acquired Taste progress and leaving you with no stun threat in the trade. He can hold Wind Wall reactively the moment you step to auto, which means you are fishing for stacks against a champion who can simply walk away through minions on his dash. Play for CS, bait the Wind Wall on a predicted Tongue Lash bluff, then throw the real one into a 25-second cooldown at rank 1. At six Devour arrives, but it does not win this duel alone while Yasuo builds into crit.

edits.before: Once Yasuo completes Infinity Edge alongside Immortal Shieldbow, the calculus flips. His crit Steel Tempest crits you through Thick Skin faster than grey health regenerates, and Last Breath's knockup duration means he can set up his own team for follow-up even if you try to Devour him mid-air. Your job is no longer to duel him — it is to peel your carries with Devour and use Abyssal Voyage to be in the right teamfight at the right moment. Accept the late-game loss in the 1v1 and win through position and disruption.
edits.after: Once Yasuo completes Infinity Edge alongside Immortal Shieldbow, the calculus flips. His Steel Tempest crits through Thick Skin faster than grey health regenerates. The trap nobody writes down: Abyssal Dive knocks up, and Last Breath blinks to any airborne enemy — your own W hands him a free ultimate, on you or on whoever you dived next to. Your job is no longer to duel him, it is to peel your carries with Devour. Accept the late-game loss in the 1v1 and win through position and disruption.

notes: Weakest entry in my slice and it got the most work. Three independent classes of error: (1) Wind Wall's cooldown written as "five seconds" when it is 25/23/21/19/17s — the one number the whole lane turns on; (2) the full layer template filled the ENEMY cooldown slot with Tahm Kench's own Tongue Lash, so every "track Yasuo's ..." instruction in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and report[5] pointed at the player's own Q — worth checking whether this template mis-fill hit other matchups and other champions; (3) the full layer invented a mechanic, "Melee on 3 stacks — Wind Wall won't matter for the stun", which flatly contradicts the content layer and has no basis in Riot's text. Also note the packet's 4 suspectNames here are all false positives, while none of the three real errors above were detected.
